AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Aim of this study was to evaluate the role of surgery plus radiotherapy in Metastatic Epidural Spinal Cord Compression (MESCC) breast cancer (BC) patients with a follow-up longer than 10 years.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Twenty-three patients treated between 2004 and 2008 were included. Surgical treatment was performed in patients with good performance status, limited metastatic disease and progressive neurologic deficit and/or intractable pain. RT was performed delivering a median total dose of 30 Gy in 10 fractions. Clinical outcome was evaluated using the modified visual-analog-scale (VAS) for pain, the Frankel scale (FS) for neurologic deficit, and MRI before, after treatments and every 3 months thereafter.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Minimal resection was performed in 17.4% of patients, curettage in 47.8%, and total tumorectomy in 34.8% followed by radiotherapy in 78.3%. Pain remission was obtained in 98% of patients and recovery of neurologic function in 92.9%. The median follow-up time was 153 months (range 128-209 months). No relapse in site of treatments occurred. The median OS time, 2, 5, and 10 years OS rates were 47 months (95%CI 33-114 months), 81% (±8.6%), 42.9% (±10.8%), and 28.6% (±9.9%). On univariate analysis performance status, kind of surgical resection, BC phenotype, and presence of other bone metastases were recorded as influencing survival, the latter confirmed also in multivariate ones.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The present update confirmed that surgery plus radiotherapy is a safe and feasible treatment with limited morbidity. In selected patients with good performance status, positive hormonal receptors, and limited metastatic disease, surgically intervention should be strongly considered ab initio.
